items.text: In addition to the new playable character Phoenix Cyclops and additional DLC costumes, we have made various fixes and adjustments to improve the gameplay experience.
Added the new playable character, Phoenix Cyclops.
Added his battle music “Fallen Phoenix,” lobby avatar, profile customization items, and gallery content.
Added the “PHOENIX CYCLOPS” Arena Course to All-Star Arena, and the Phoenix Cyclops Support Soul to Survival in All-Star Arena.
Added the Phoenix Cyclops Fighter Soul to Arcadia Rumble.
These items are available in each mode after purchasing either the MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls Ultimate Edition, Digital Deluxe Edition, the Year 1 Character & Stage Pass or Phoenix Cyclops DLC.
Added the Benchmark Test feature to check the game’s performance within your PC environment before playing online.
Players that pass the benchmark may use this as a filter in online matchmaking to play with others who have also passed it.
The shader warmup is now required upon launching the game.
Made adjustments to improve the stability and consistency of online matches, helping reduce unexpected interruptions and disruptions during gameplay for the PC version.
Made adjustments to improve online match stability and reduce unexpected disruptions during gameplay.
Implemented an icon to indicate slowdown during online matches on the player or opponent side.
Fixed an issue causing desynchronization issues to occur sometimes while spectating online matches.
Fixed an issue causing the game to become unresponsive when attempting to spectate in the Open Lobby or Room Matches under certain conditions.
Fixed an issue causing the match results to differ from the actual match during replay playback in rare instances.
Fixed an issue causing unintended controls to be possible during playback.
Expanded the search range when selecting “Nearby Regions” under the Region Settings.
It remains possible to avoid matching with players with incompatible network connections by using the “Connection Speed” option.
This adjustment will make it easier to find matches, especially if you have set the “Connection Speed” restrictions low.
When selecting “All” under the Region Settings, “Connection Speed” restrictions no longer apply.
This adjustment skips unnecessary checks regarding connection strength, providing the fast matchmaking expected of the “All” region option.

If you prefer to prioritize matchmaking with strong network connections, please set the “Connection Speed” restriction with your Region Settings adjusted to either “Same Area Only” or “Nearby Regions.”
When this patch is applied, the Platform Settings will be reset to the default setting, “All.”
As the performance of the PC version has been improved, this reset intends to provide a better matchmaking environment.
If you prefer to match with only the same platform, please choose the “Same Platform Only” option from the Matching Settings.
Added an item to the Matching Settings providing the choice to limit your matchmaking only to players who meet the performance standards from the benchmark test.
Revised the rating fluctuation calculations for the Master rank.
Adjusted the conditions to move from Vibranium to Master.
We had set the conditions to rank up from Vibranium to Master to be highly challenging, but this resulted in fewer players reaching Master rank than anticipated.
This led to longer wait times for matches as well as matches between players with a large difference in rating within the Master rank.
To provide the intended, smooth matchmaking experience for more players, we have changed the conditions as follows.
Rank Up Conditions Before Change: 4 wins out of 5 matches
Rank Up Conditions After Change: 3 wins out of 5 matches
Our goal with this change is to achieve the intended number of players active in Master rank, making it easier to find opponents and match with players closer to your level.
Set a limit on the difference in rating between players in Master Ranked Matches.
To preserve the concept of matching with players close to your current level, we have set a limit to prevent players from matching with others of a rating greatly above or below their own.
This adjustment aims to provide fair matchmaking by avoiding matches with an extreme gap in player ability.
We expect the impact on matchmaking speed for all players to be very minimal.
Fixed an issue where even when the rank-up challenge was failed, the rank-up matches would not end and the remaining matches would play out.
Fixed an issue causing rating fluctuation to occur when rematching a Vibranium player directly after the rank-up match to go from Vibranium to Master rank.
A pop-up will now be displayed to indicate the Room Code when creating a room after setting a Room Code.
After selecting Disband Room or Exit Room, you will now transition to the Battle Menu.
Added “Assist Cooldown” item to the Gauge Settings within the Training Menu.
Added “Playback Method” item for the Recreate Battle State feature within the Training Menu.

In this patch, we have made adjustments to game mechanics and addressed issues with characters. For game mechanic adjustments, we have taken into account the requests from the in-game survey along with the expectations of the development team. We have extended the cooldown for calling Assists, increased the regain values of the Assemble Gauge, and improved the responsiveness for various inputs.

For the increase to Assemble Gauge gain values, the extended cooldown would result in gaining less Assemble Gauge if kept as-is, so we have adjusted to ensure a similar rate of Assemble Gauge will be gained as in the current version.
The concept behind the game mechanic adjustments is to maintain the current battle mechanics while somewhat reducing the amount of information on the screen at one time and improving legibility.

While the moments of spontaneous chaos in matches are intended, currently the frequency of calling Assists and tagging is higher than anticipated, creating situations where the screen is overly busy or the match loses momentum.
We have made these adjustments after seeing players also requested to extend the cooldown and decrease the frequency of Assists, in alignment with the concept described above.

As a result of the reduced frequency of calling Assists, the player will need to play neutral either solo or with fewer Assists more often. This creates more variation throughout the match, moving from strings using Assists to fighting either solo or with fewer Assists, while also improving legibility.

While we have not made direct character adjustments, as a result of mechanic adjustments and fixes for issues, there are several impacts on the characters in battle such as making the Champion more powerful. Please refer to the character section for more details.

The link to the survey page is available from the in-game top page. Sharing your opinions and impressions, as well as reporting issues, helps improve the game’s development. Your feedback is always greatly appreciated.

Thanks to everyone in our community who participated in last year’s closed beta tests. One of the team’s goals was to better understand how players interacted with the game’s mechanics and overall pacing, including tempo, character switches, and overall gameplay flow.

The team received a great amount of feedback that directed several gameplay improvements. We’re excited to share what those major changes are and will be reflected for fans to enjoy at upcoming events starting at AWT Finals.
The following are the list of changes.
Note: The button labels in this article are for the PS5 version.

notes.title: ▶Removed member change functions with assemble button; assigned previous Quick Tag Button as dedicated Tag Button

items.text: 【Tag Button （L2）】
・Enabled during pre-battle, direct call during match, on Assist Attack hit and during the pause before Assist withdraw.
→Since this button is dedicated to member change functions, it does not do anything when pressed during Assemble Smash for follow-up attacks.
・Direct tag out functions the same as the previous Quick Tag (QT) button: as soon as character enters screen.
→However, if a different assist is called or if the point character takes damage during entry, that assist will withdraw without doing anything, only going through the member change animation.
・Sped up the Member Change animation from 30 frames to 20 frames to increase the overall tempo.
【Assemble Button （✕）】

・Removed all functions related to member change and reassigned to Tag Button. As an exception, Super Assemble (X during Super Skill) is the only time when member change happens as a result of pressing X.
Players felt that it was hard to distinguish between Assist and member change and that unintended member changes occurred due to it being assigned to the same button as Assist.
We originally intended to minimize the required number of buttons, but we have concluded that minimizing unintended inputs was more important.
In addition to L, M, H, Unique, Assemble, we added the Tag button for a total of 6 buttons.
Since the Tag button is dedicated to member change, member changes will no longer occur unless the player presses the Tag button with the clear intent of executing member change.

notes.title: ▶Changed screen freeze duration during member change.

items.text: To improve game tempo, we have changed the animation from 30 frames to 20 frames, allowing for a smoother transition to the next character.

notes.title: ▶Reduced screen freeze duration when calling Assist via cancelling.

items.text: On trigger, screen freeze will occur as with Assemble Rush, but will cut out frames of the entry portion of the animation.
In addition, the assist character will now appear from behind the main character when using Cancel Assist and is also sped up accordingly with the screen freeze time adjustment.
The above applies when the main character is in the air (cancel air attack with ↓+X to trigger Vertical Assist).
We decided to implement this change because one of the most requested changes during the CBT was the ability to call an assist via cancelling an attack.
In addition, we reduced the entry animation, and the screen freeze time has also been reduced from 20 to 10 frames.
During CBT, it was noted that the screen freeze during Assemble Rush (Assist called by cancelling) and the screen freeze when calling one type of Assist looked the same.
The above changes are meant to resolve this issue and as a result, the game should grant players more freedom and combo variety.
Some players during CBT voiced the opinion that Assemble Rush was not needed at all, but we still believe that this mechanic is a necessary feature.
In this project, we want to make sure that the player understands the exact timing to which their assist characters will execute the attack after pressing a button.

If players were able to call an Assist whenever they wanted, it would become unclear when they should press the button. It will also lead to missed execution due to slight differences in button press timing.
Therefore, Assemble Rush exists as an easier way to utilize the Assist mechanic.
Based on the added cancel trigger of Shooter, Vertical and Assault Assists, Assault Rush now triggers only when the directional lever is in neutral position.
In this case, the character that enters the screen is prioritized the same way as Assemble Smash: in the order of availability.
The commands are listed below.
Neutral ＋× Assemble Assist (Shooter).
→＋× Assemble Assist (Shooter).
↓＋× Assemble Assist (Vertical).
←＋× Assemble Assist （Assault）.
Neutral ＋× Assemble Rush （prioritizes entry in order of standby character number 2＞3＞4）
→＋× Assemble Assist (Shooter).
↓＋× Assemble Assist (Vertical).
←＋× Assemble Assist （Assault）.

notes.title: ▶Consecutive Assists can now be triggered with neutral+X.

items.text: With the addition of a dedicated Tag button, players can now trigger consecutive assists with neutral + X input.
Assist characters will enter the screen in the order of their slot placement (2→3→4). This change allows for a smoother execution experience when calling assists consecutively.
This is in response to players wanting to use ground Assists while in the air.
We observed instances where an aerial Assist would trigger even though the Assist was called just before jumping. This change improves upon the accuracy of inputs as well as strategic freedom.
Aerial Assists trigger when the main character is positioned higher than a normal jump height (slightly higher than normal jump, double jump height or high jump height).
Aerial Assists mainly consist of attacks that are directed toward the ground.
As a basic rule of this game, the Assist character attacks once the character appears fully onscreen.
We do not necessarily reject the idea of attacking from offscreen, but as a basic policy, we want characters to appear fully onscreen before attacking.
However, we do understand Assist characters attacking from offscreen as a result of the main character moving after the Assist was called.
Thus in general, players cannot trigger ground Assists from a high altitude.
However, if the mechanic becomes pointless, players will stop using it, hence the above change.
Aerial Assist movement ranges greatly, so this change should give players more strategic freedom.

notes.title: ▶Sub character attacks are now all high attacks.

items.text: Including Assist attacks, this also applies to member changes triggered after executing an overhead attack.
Although technically, players can pre-emptively evade unblockable setups using Assemble Counter or Crossover, the previous changes made unblockable setups too easy, hence this change.
This is a nerf to Link Attacks.
When Standing L whiffs, the Link Attack L no longer triggers.
This eliminates instances where a character tracks the opponent character when crossed up.
Players during CBT commented that Link Attacks unintentionally triggers, so we made changes to improve input accuracy.
Link Attack finishes now trigger only when directional input is neutral or forward.
This will eliminate cases where Link Attacks trigger when crouch-attacking, for example.

notes.title: ▶Adjustment to Link Attack limit to a maximum of four Links

items.text: Link Attack performs a series of multiple normal moves. As this would often be used against a blocking opponent, it resulted in matches sometimes feeling long. We have changed how the normal move part of Link Attack functions to increase the tempo of the offensive and defensive turns throughout a match. We have adjusted it so that L, M, and H normal moves can only be included in a Link Attack up to 4 times. This makes strings such as L > L > M > H or Standing M > Crouching M > Standing H > Crouching H possible. Each character's Unique attacks are not affected by this change.

notes.title: ▶Adjustment so only single button route Link Attacks combo into Skills

items.text: Pressure strings could be extended due to how each normal move could continue into a Link Attack route to combo into a Skill. To address this, we have adjusted this so that Link Attack routes that combo into Skills will only trigger when pressing the same attack button. It is limited to the following routes: L > L > L (Link Attack finisher) > L ~ H Skill > Super Skill or Ultimate Skill M > M (Link Attack finisher) > L ~ H Skill > Super Skill or Ultimate Skill H > H (Link Attack finisher) > L ~ H Skill > Super Skill or Ultimate Skill

notes.title: ▶Super Skills no longer cause Wall Break.

items.text: During CBT, Super Skills triggered Wall Breaks that resulted in stage transition. However, this animation was long and affected the overall tempo of the game.
We want to minimize timeframes where the game does not accept any inputs or where the players are just watching the screen, hence this change.

notes.title: ▶Post-Wall Break, the receiving end is in full knockdown, instead of neutral with opponent.

items.text: During CBT, both sides went back to neutral after wall break. Players felt dissatisfied that the situation returned to neutral despite the player who triggered the break having taken the advantage.
Furthermore, if the receiver turns things around and triggers another wall break, it ruins the tempo of the game.
In line with the previous removal of Super Skill Wall Beaks, this change also aims to improve game tempo.
With this buff to Wall Breaks, the match flow should feel better and Wall Break frequency mitigated.
After wall break, the receiving end will now be in untechable knockdown state. The initiator of the wall break now has a +25 frame advantage, instead of the previous 0 frame.

notes.title: ▶Reduced combo limit consumption of aerial normals by half.

items.text: During CBT, combos reached their limit at odd timings, preventing players to complete a full combo and leading to an unsatisfying experience.
Since air combos see frequent usage, this change allows players to enjoy combos better.
Damage output and minimum proration values have been adjusted accordingly.
This is a bonus that influences the minimum proration when multiple skills are used.
Simply put, the more variety of attacks used in a combo, the higher the damage output.
This change makes it easier to perform a jump cancel while a button is tapped repeatedly.
During CBT, attack buttons took priority, making it difficult to perform jump cancels.
This is another change to address input accuracy.
Homing jump was triggered when an attack button was pressed after a crouching H during a combo, but it also now triggers from a Jump input.
The character will move to the opponent’s position smoothly when going for a combo.
If opting to perform a normal jump instead, you can input Jump while holding down the H button.

notes.title: While guarding, chip damage is now converted to healing gauge.

items.text: The above changes will give players more strategic options around dealing and healing damage.
